questions.architecture: The pure core is untouched. The format change uses no timers, clock or DOM; module-level hexEnd is synchronous scratch state, not shared across awaits. No public API change: the new functions are module-private and subsetFontGaps keeps its signature, with only a doc addition. There is no file-format change: reading a loose field more strictly is reader policy, and ADR-0201's field is unchanged. No new runtime dependency. The new workflow pins its actions by SHA, sets persist-credentials false and contents: read. Its toolchain comes from an emsdk git tag plus emsdk's download, not a commit pin (F2).

The landed commit is 78a8aae: authored 2026-10-27, committed 2026-10-30 17:15Z on rebase. 5d5c767 filled the cell with the pre-rebase sha, and 0ded9c1 left it. A scan of every M18 Commit cell finds this as the only bad one. scripts/gates/check-digest.mjs:147-158 (commitCellProblems) only flags an empty cell, so check-digest --head --full-history prints '204 M18 task commits have tracked review evidence and Commit cells'.
findings.failure_scenario: Rebase-before-land is routine here, so any row whose cell is filled from a local sha before landing ends up citing an unreachable commit. The completion gate's Commit-cell leg passes anyway, and a later reviewer or `git show <cell>` cannot find the change the row claims.

findings.evidence: The rebuild clones emsdk with `--branch 6.0.13` (a mutable tag) and runs `emsdk install 6.0.13`, which downloads a prebuilt toolchain. build-font-engine.mjs:43 checks only the version number from `emcc --version` (/\) (\d+\.\d+\.\d+) \(/), and ignores the revision that the same line prints in parentheses. The manifest pins toolchain.emscriptenRevision e13ee988ce3d87a738dd8f3661d02223308c412a, but nothing reads it. check-font-engine-evidence compares the manifest's toolchain object between the run's commit and now, so the record stays valid whatever compiler the tag resolved to.
findings.failure_scenario: The evidence row claims a pinned-toolchain rebuild, but the pin that names the compiler build is never compared. A rebuild that matches the committed bytes still shows that the bytes come from the pinned sources. The fail-open case is narrow: a retagged or substituted emsdk 6.0.13 that also produced the committed bytes. But the record cannot say which compiler it used, and any later rebuild under a moved tag is red for a reason the log does not name.

findings.evidence: The writer records unicodeRangeOf(coveredBy(asset, inventory)). The inventory may hold up to 0x110000 scalars (font-subset.ts:158), and nothing caps the written string. An inventory of about 250k non-adjacent scalars writes more than 2 000 000 chars, which the new reader then treats as unreadable.
findings.failure_scenario: The studio's own subset save of a pathological document then reports every character as a gap on the next save. This fails safe (a whole-font re-cut and a spurious warning), and no realistic text gets there.
